henry.title: Harvest Dance Rhythms
henry.intro: Harvest festivals have music with strong beats. A rhythm is a pattern of sounds and quiet spaces.
steps: Compose a 'harvest dance' in Song Maker.
worksheet: Write your rhythm with X for a beat and - for quiet (8 boxes).
What did changing the tempo do?
Describe your harvest dance in 3 words.
Draw a picture of a fall festival with music.
Write your rhythm with X for a beat and - for quiet.
What happened when you changed the tempo?
links: Tap the dots to make the monkeys drum, then press ▶.
Click squares to add notes for your harvest dance, then press ▶.

steps: Click the dots to turn beats on (orange) or off.
Press ▶ to hear the monkeys drum your pattern.
Click the → arrow to try other drummers.
0.look: Make a pattern that repeats, like a harvest dance.
0.q: Write your rhythm with X for a beat and - for quiet.

steps: Click squares on the grid to add notes. Higher = higher sound.
Press the big blue ▶ to play your song.
Drag the Tempo slider to go faster or slower. Click Marimba to change instruments.
1.look: Try a low, bouncy part at the bottom and a tune on top.
1.q: What happened when you changed the tempo?

frankie.title: Falling Leaves Song
frankie.intro: Fall leaves are red, orange, and yellow. Let's draw leaves and hear them sing!
steps: Draw leaves in Kandinsky and press play.
worksheet: Clap: leaf, leaf, fall-ing! How many claps? ___
Draw your singing leaf on your paper 🍁
links: Draw leaves with your finger, then tap ▶ to hear them sing!

0.look: Grown-up: draw a circle together and it gets a face that sings!
0.q: Draw your singing leaf on your paper 🍁
